description: Normalized public market data for euroflex-bess-lab; see README.md and LICENSES.md.

files.title: Belgian aFRR capacity auction awards aggregated per delivery block and direction.
transformation_notes: Sources: ODS125 (individual aFRR capacity bids up to 19/05/2026, one row per bid with up and down columns) and ODS207 (as of 20/05/2026, one row per bid and regulation direction). Where both cover a delivery day, ODS207 wins.
One row per delivery block (4 hours, Europe/Brussels local time, converted to UTC; 3/5 hours on DST-change days) and direction (up/down). Prices are capacity prices in EUR/MW/h (pay-as-bid).

Bids whose delivery period spans several 4-hour blocks (e.g. '0 - 24' daily bids) deliver in every block they cover, so they are counted in each covered block; awarded_mw_multi_block shows that share.

awarded_mw = sum of awarded MW; vwap_eur_per_mw_h = awarded-volume-weighted average bid price; marginal_eur_per_mw_h = highest awarded bid price; n_bids = number of bids with awarded MW > 0; offered_mw / n_offered_bids describe all offered bids (selected or not) delivering in the block; they are null where the source lists awarded bids only (ODS055, i.e. mFRR before 2026-05-20).
Gate-2 bids ('G2' suffix in capacitybiddeliveryperiod) are treated like other bids of their period.

files.title: Merit-order curves of available aFRR/mFRR energy bids per quarter-hour on a fixed MW grid.
transformation_notes: Built from ODS156 (incremental = direction up) and ODS157 (decremental = direction down) individual energy bids; only bids with availability == 'Available' are used. Raw bid rows are not redistributed.
Bid volumes are the increments of Elia's published cumulativevolume in its merit-order rank, so bids that add no volume (mutually exclusive alternatives, unavailable bids) are excluded.

Per quarter-hour and direction the available aFRR + mFRR (+ reserve-sharing) bids are sorted by price into an economic merit order: cheapest first for up (incremental), highest price first for down (decremental). price_eur_mwh at cum_mw = V is the price of the bid that covers the V-th MW, i.e. the marginal price needed to activate V MW. Null where the available volume is below V. Grid: 0..2000 MW in 25 MW steps.
Elia's own rank (aFRR first, then mFRR) was tested as an alternative ordering and tracks the published MIP/MDP much worse (see validation.curve_vs_published_prices for the price-sorted curve).

Approximation: real aFRR activations are continuous and priced via PICASSO cross-border marginal prices, mFRR via MARI, and Elia may skip bids (e.g. for congestion); treat the curve as a stylised local merit order for price-impact studies, not as the settlement price.

files.title: Pre-MARI per-minute imbalance prices (2023-01 to 2024-05-21), legacy layout.
transformation_notes: Pre-MARI Elia data (before the 22/05/2024 MARI local go-live), kept separate because the price formula and field set differ from the current tables. timestamp_utc = interval start (UTC).

imbalance_price_long_eur_mwh / imbalance_price_short_eur_mwh = Elia positive / negative imbalance price (applied to long / short BRPs); they are identical from 2020 on (single pricing). imbalance_price_eur_mwh (QH) and price_cum_eur_mwh (minute) repeat the long-side price for convenience.
Minute rows (ODS046) are cumulative quarter-hour-to-date estimates like ODS133; calculation_time_utc is Elia's calculation timestamp. nrv = net regulation volume.
Numeric columns float32; reindexed to a complete grid between the first and last published interval.

files.title: Per-minute imbalance price (cumulative QH-to-date), SI/ACE/volumes and price components.
transformation_notes: timestamp_utc = start of the minute (UTC). ODS133/ODS165 label the minute at the end of which the estimate was computed: the row hh:mm includes all events of the running quarter-hour up to hh:mm:59, so it becomes usable at hh:mm+1 plus publication lag.

ODS133 columns (*_cum_*, mip/mdp/alpha/price_cum) are cumulative quarter-hour-to-date estimates; the row at minute 14 of a quarter-hour equals the final quarter-hour value (see validation.last_minute_vs_qh).
ODS126 columns (si_mw, ace_mw, *_up_mw, *_down_mw, rs_*) are instantaneous minute values.
ODS165 duplicates of ODS133 (systemimbalance, ace, marginal prices) are dropped; quality_status is ODS133's.
Rows are reindexed to a complete 1-minute grid between the first and last minute seen in any source; minutes missing upstream are null (counts in validation).
Numeric columns are float32; timestamps datetime64[ns, UTC].
ODS134 was read only to validate the last minute of each QH against the final price.

files.title: Elia simulation of the new 2026 imbalance-price formula, per minute (Jan-Jul 2026).
transformation_notes: Elia simulation of the imbalance price under the new formula consulted for go-live on 24/11/2026 (conditional on CREG approval), computed on historical data for 2026-01..2026-07. Best-effort, non-validated data; Elia removes it from ODS211/ODS212 on 17/11/2026, this file preserves it.

Minute rows are cumulative quarter-hour-to-date estimates like ODS133: at minute 14 FRCE equals the ODS212 value and the price matches in about 95% of quarter-hours, the SI estimate differs (see validation.last_minute_vs_ods212). frce_rolling_mw / si_rolling_mw are 15-minute rolling windows that reach back past the start of the quarter-hour.

imbalance_price = main_up (SI < 0) or main_down (SI >= 0); when incentive_eur_mwh is published (only when FRCE exceeds the L2 target and |SI| > 250 MW) the price is max(main_up, incentive) for a short system and min(main_down, incentive) for a long system (53 of 53 incentive quarter-hours); main components are volume-weighted aFRR/mFRR prices with weights weight_afrr/weight_mfrr (decomposition match rates in validation.decomposition of the QH file).
Numeric columns float32; timestamps datetime64[ns, UTC]; reindexed to a complete grid between the first and last published interval.

files.title: Belgian load, wind and PV measured + forecast per quarter-hour.
transformation_notes: timestamp_utc = start of the quarter-hour (UTC); values in MW (Elia publishes MW averages per QH).

load_* from ODS001 (total load on the Belgian grid incl. estimated losses); wind_* are sums over all ODS031 rows (offshore + onshore, Elia- and DSO-connected, all regions); pv_* are the ODS032 region 'Belgium' rows.

Forecast vintages: *_da_11h_* = day-ahead forecast published 11:00 D-1 (usable before the 12:00 CET day-ahead gate); *_da_forecast_* = day-ahead forecast published 18:00 D-1 (after the DA auction); *_week_ahead_*; *_most_recent_* = latest revision before delivery (look-ahead risk for anything but near-real-time use: its issue time is not published).
P10/P90 bands are dropped (they are not additive across regions).

files.title: Elia SI forecast for the current quarter-hour, issued every minute.
transformation_notes: prediction_time_utc = time the forecast was made (Elia `predictiontimeutc`, one forecast per minute); target_qh_utc = start of the quarter-hour whose average SI is forecast.
ODS136 targets the running quarter-hour, ODS147 the next one. Probabilities are for the target-QH average SI falling in [-inf,-400], [-400,-200], [-200,0], [0,200], [200,400], [400,inf] MW.
prediction_quality = Elia `predictionquality` (share of input data available, in percent).
Only contract columns are kept (resolutioncode and the ODS147 plotting helper column are dropped).

files.title: Belgian day-ahead auction prices (hourly until 2025-09-30, 15-minute afterwards).
transformation_notes: timestamp_utc = start of the day-ahead product; resolution_minutes = product length inferred from the spacing of consecutive timestamps (60 until delivery day 2025-09-30, 15 from 2025-10-01 after the SDAC 15-minute MTU go-live).
Monthly API requests (local delivery days, end inclusive) are concatenated and de-duplicated on timestamp_utc; null prices are dropped. price_eur_mwh is float32.

files.title: ECB euro foreign exchange reference rate, GBP per EUR (daily).
files.fetch_command: euroflex data gb fetch fx  (or: .venv/bin/python scripts/research/gb_fetch_data.py --target fx)
files.source: European Central Bank data portal (data-api.ecb.europa.eu), series EXR.D.GBP.EUR.SP00.A
files.licence: ECB terms of use (free reuse with source citation)
files.licence_terms: Free use of information obtained from the ECB website provided it appears accurately and the ECB is cited as the source; modifications (here: as-of join of daily rates onto delivery dates) must be stated.
files.attribution: Source: European Central Bank (euro foreign exchange reference rates)
transformation_notes: timestamp_utc = reference date 00:00 UTC (rates are set around 16:00 CET on TARGET business days).
gbp_per_eur = OBS_VALUE (pound sterling per euro). Consumers as-of join the latest rate dated on or before each delivery date (forward fill over weekends and holidays).

files.attribution: Contains BMRS data © Elexon Limited copyright and database right 2023-2026
files.method_reference: NESO Response Services Service Terms, Schedule 2 Table 1 and para 6.7 (delivery curves)
transformation_notes: For each SP and product (DCL, DCH, DML, DMH, DRL, DRH): MWh delivered per MW contracted = mean over the SP's 15-second samples of the product's delivery fraction x 0.5 h (sample-and-hold).

Delivery curves: deadband +/-0.015 Hz; DC 5 % at +/-0.2 Hz and 100 % at +/-0.5 Hz; DM 5 % at +/-0.1 Hz and 100 % at +/-0.2 Hz; DR linear to 100 % at +/-0.2 Hz; linear interpolation, saturation beyond.
Low products export (frequency below 50 Hz), high products import; values are non-negative.
SPs with fewer than 60 of 120 samples are NaN. freq_* columns are per-SP statistics of the deviation from 50 Hz in mHz; share_outside_200mhz is the share of samples with |deviation| > 0.2 Hz.
15-second sampling misses sub-15-second excursions (mostly relevant for DC); this is an approximation of the 1-second performance-monitoring view.
